To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction of IL-6 with TNF-α in the diabetic heart contributes to endothelial cell dysfunction through a mechanism that includes increased oxidative stress and decreased endothelial nitric oxide synthase activation.
the interactions between TNF and IL-6 contribute to endothelial dysfunction by increasing oxidative stress and reducing eNOS phosphorylation in coronary arterioles of type 2 diabetic mice.
the interactions between TNF and IL-6 contribute to endothelial dysfunction by reducing the phosphorylation of e-NOS and increasing oxidative stress in coronary arterioles in type 2 diabetes mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of IL-6 with other cytokines in the development of cardiovascular disease in T2D.
the interaction of IL-6/TNF-α in the pathogenesis of coronary endothelial dysfunction.
a better understanding of the role of inflammatory cytokines, such IL-6 and/or TNF-α, in coronary endothelial dysfunction of type 2 diabetes, and the possible therapeutic targets for the treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactions between TNF-alpha and IL-6 contribute to coronary arteriole dysfunction in T2DM mice by reducing eNOS phosphorylation and increasing superoxide production.
IL-6 and its interaction with TNF-α are important contributors to coronary endothelial function in obesity and T2D.
the interaction between TNF- α and IL-6 contributes to the development of coronary endothelial dysfunction and may be a potential therapeutic target for T2D.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interactions between TNF and IL-6 are important for the development of endothelial dysfunction in coronary arterioles from diabetic hearts.
the interactions between TNF and IL-6 contribute to coronary endothelial cell dysfunction by promoting oxidative stress and impairing eNOS phosphorylation.

the interactions of TNF- and IL-6 in T2D contribute to endothelial dysfunction by increasing oxidative stress and reducing eNOS phosphorylation, and these effects can be attenuated by anti-IL6 treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor (TNF) have a reciprocal relationship, and their interaction contributes to the development of coronary endothelial dysfunction.
IL-6 and its interactions with other cytokines, such TNF, may be a therapeutic target for coronary endothelial dysfunction.
the inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, and IL-6 are individually considered as major contributors to endothelial and vascular dysfunction in obesity and T2D.
